intro.heading: Getting Started
text: Our app allows you to keep track of expenses without having to manually update them!
To do this we require you to do 2 things:
Set up email transaction alerts from your own bank.
Set up auto forwarding from your email to your unique forwarding email that we assign you.

steps.heading: Find Alert Limit
text: Most banks provide email transaction alerts for transactions over a certain limit (e.g. $200). Find out how to change the transaction alert limit.

steps.heading: Change Alert Limit
text: Change the transaction alert limit to $0. This ensures you receive an email for every transaction.

steps.heading: Confirm Email
text: Ensure the email that receives alerts is the same email you use to sign in to our app.
notes: Since the transaction limit is set to $0, you may receive a large volume of emails.
We recommend creating a rule to move transaction alert emails into a separate folder.
After setting up forwarding and filters, you may choose 'Archive Gmail’s copy' or 'Delete Gmail’s copy' (not recommended).

steps.heading: Get Forwarding Address
text: Get your unique forwarding email address.
Sign into our app using the Sign in With Google button. Go to Settings → Your unique forwarding address and copy the address.

image.alt: Copy your unique forwarding address from app settings.

steps.heading: Open Gmail Settings
text: Open Gmail settings and click 'See all settings'.

image.alt: Open Gmail settings and click 'See all settings'.

steps.heading: Add Forwarding Email
text: Go to the 'Forwarding and POP/IMAP' tab.
Click 'Add a forwarding address' and paste your unique forwarding email.
Click Next → Proceed → OK.
notes: You will see a popup asking you to verify forwarding.

steps.heading: Confirm Forwarding
text: In our app, go to Settings and scroll to 'Your activation link'.
Click the confirmation link to confirm the forwarding address.

image.alt: Click the confirmation link to confirm the forwarding address.

steps.heading: Add Email Filter
text: Filters ensure that only transaction-related emails are forwarded.
Go to the 'Filters and Blocked Addresses' tab.
Click 'Create a new filter'.
Customize the filter using sender and subject/body wrapped in double quotes.
notes: Filter rules vary by bank. Check your transaction emails for correct content.
DBS PayLah users must create a separate filter for 'paylah.alert@dbs.com'.
If your bank has a wallet feature, remember to create a separate filter.

image.alt: An example filter for dbs bank

captions: Here is an example filter for dbs bank. The email MUST be from 'ibanking.alert@dbs.com' and the body MUST contain 'transaction was completed'.

steps.heading: Confirm filter
text: Click 'Create Filter' and select 'Forward it to' your unique forwarding email.
Click the blue 'Create Filter' button.
Verify that the filter appears in the list.

image.alt: Verify that the filter appears in the list.

testingFilter.heading: Testing Filter
text: In case it was not clear, this step is kinda important. This is because your expenses will not be tracked correctly if the filter is not working as intended.

On the Filters and Blocked Addresses page in settings, click on the 'Edit' button for the newly created filter and then click 'Search' (blue button). You should see the emails you intend to forward. Make sure to do this for all filters! (Example for both ibanking and paylah alerts filter mentioned before).

warning.heading: Do Not Forward All Emails
text: Forwarding all your emails will result in loss of privacy for you and server overload (and subsequently dropping your requests) for us.
To prevent this, select the 'Disable Forwarding' option.
